## Result

- Skill: delivery-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Package members: primary plan, docs/plans/2026-09-08-skill-model-proposal-family-pilot.md. Remaining subjects are assessment basis, not additional Delivery package members.
- Upstream review ID: design-review-r2.
- Review ID and round: delivery-review-r2, round 2.
- Traceability result: sufficient allocation of SKL-SR-01–23, SKL-DEC-01–05 and SYS-SR-02/04/06/07 for the scoped Skill-owner/pilot interaction, including the current-candidate metadata dependency.
- Material findings: none.
- Correction targets: none.
- Recording status: recorded upon successful primary review-record persistence.
- Open blockers: none.
- Immediate next stage: isolated stop; return to route for separately authorized continuation.
- Claim limitations: exact Delivery package approval only; no implementation, initialized work, generated candidate, source retirement/adoption, milestone completion, final Code Review, Verify, publication or customer installation is established.

## Independence, freshness and reuse

The parent plan author made the user-requested engineering corrections. Independent agent /root/independent_delivery_review authored none of the plan, Design or clarification note and made no engineering edits. This reviewer performed the earlier independent Delivery assessment and now reread the entire revised primary plan and clarification note for a fresh package judgment.

The inspected current plan identity is sha256:5f1f00d9e756e084670fb0acf094f7f45a25a850fbc1de88f9ea4fd0cd9260c4. Full primary subject inspection binds 50 subjects. Comparing the 49 round-1 basis subjects identifies only the plan and plan-authoring evidence record as changed; the clarification note is newly added. All 35 upstream Design Review subjects are unchanged. Current scoped context is complete, design-review-r2 remains current and approved, delivery-review-r1 is correctly restricted to stale applicability, and skl-dr-001 remains resolved by its original reporter. No open selected blocker prevents this assessment.

Round-1 source inspections and unchanged-scope findings remain usable because the correction changes proof allocation and explicit System traceability without changing engineering requirements, source dispositions, scope, production mechanisms or governance. This reuse covers the unchanged facts and criteria analysis documented in round 1, not its old plan approval or old authoring-check pass. The reviewer reassessed the full revised plan and its combined effect below. The earlier judgment and exact subjects remain unchanged.

## Corrections assessed

The plan now makes candidate-metadata dependency inspection an explicit M1 step, TG-03 required outcome and Validation-plan item. If changed package bytes affect current-candidate metadata or dependent assertions, the implementer must identify affected paths, the existing owning builder and direct checks, regenerate through that builder and validate before milestone closure. An unaffected conclusion requires inspected evidence. Archive generation alone cannot satisfy this obligation. Historical releases, invented hashes, version bumps, publication and a new release-verification gate remain outside scope.

This is a real producer/consumer dependency: scripts/test-adapter-distribution.py's test_v0_5_1_bundled_candidate_metadata_matches_generated_route_only_archives compares bundled current-candidate metadata against metadata derived from generated archives. scripts/adapter_distribution.py contains the existing _local_release_candidate_metadata construction and local candidate metadata/index writing path. Those inspected mechanisms make the allocation feasible; implementation still selects the exact affected current-candidate builder and directly dependent checks from its then-current dependency inspection. No metadata was generated or modified for this review, and no historical release rewrite is approved.

The new requirements row and TG-FINAL-01 explicitly allocate SYS-SR-02/04/06/07 only to the approved Skill-owner/pilot amendment. They match System's actual meanings: shared owner/consumer references, coherent affected producer/consumer behavior, separation of current truth/work/judgments/history, and bounded migration with named remainder. M1/TG-02–03 observes pilot procedure, validator and candidate interactions; M2/TG-04–05 observes ownership, historical separation and receiving owners; TG-FINAL-01 assesses their composed result. This adds no unrelated System extraction, implementation milestone, customer installation or inventory-wide adoption.

## Complete revised package assessment

| Criterion | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Safe dependency order and intermediate states | M1 still couples the four pilot content files to profile/placement validation, canonical regression checks, archive comparisons and now explicit current-candidate metadata reconciliation. M2 requires independently assessed pilot value before conditional source transfer. No moved-heading bypass or metadata mismatch may be treated as a complete M1 result. |
| Requirements and architecture trace | SKL-SR-01–23 and all five decisions retain their M1/M2 and local/integrated proof mappings. The scoped System requirements now have explicit traceability. The eight Design dimensions and four composed hazards retain production-boundary or independent semantic observation, including portable/adopted policy coexistence and source-owner duplication. |
| Normal, negative and integrated proof | TG-01 retains usable ordinary/governed authoring and advisory/formal review walkthroughs, malformed/late-trigger/resource/authority stops and independent usefulness judgment. TG-02 rejects selected-resource and dispatch defects without relying on unrelated words. TG-03 covers all supported candidates, non-pilot byte preservation and metadata consistency. TG-04/05 assess complete transferred rules, preserved protection, original bytes, usable links and remaining ownership. TG-FINAL-01 observes final combined subjects and consumers. |
| Migration, authority and recovery | Four source snapshots and three explicitly historical source-path retentions remain the approved bounded disposition. Mixed specialist/operational sources retain their owners. Coupled rollback regenerates derived output and preserves failed evidence and judgments; actual semantic gaps return to the owning author. No package pass, review save or installation grants adoption or publication authority. |
| Proportional proof and maintenance | Production selection and supported archive boundaries remain observable. Replaced wording oracles need equivalent useful protection first; historical proof policy is not reactivated. New metadata allocation adds a directly affected dependency check rather than a universal release gate or target-agent benchmark. |
| Closeout and evidence applicability | Both milestones and required corrections still precede fresh independent final whole-change Code Review, followed by distinct Verify. Local group passes cannot substitute. Reuse requires an affirmative unchanged-surface/environment basis; affected metadata/check subjects invalidate relevant earlier passes. |

No material defect or missing necessary owner decision was identified in the revised complete package. Round 1's other adequacy conclusions remain supported by unchanged subjects and the full-plan reread; this is a new approval of the revised identity, not renewal of the old record.

## Checks and limitations

Actually performed: complete revised-plan and clarification-note reads; bounded System requirement and candidate-metadata builder/assertion source inspections using cat/sed/rg; full primary scoped context; subject inspect --content full --max-bytes 8388608 for 50 subjects; comparison with round-1 subjects; and primary targeted review recording. Searches also named nonexistent scripts/build-release-artifact-metadata.py and packages/rigorloop/scripts; their errors were observed, actual paths were located through repository search, and no conclusion relies on them.

The updated plan-authoring evidence binds this revision and records passing validate-documentation-prose.py, validate-markdown-readability.py, local-link checks and git diff --check, with 54 advisory readability warnings. Those author checks were inspected, not rerun by the reviewer, and do not substitute for this semantic assessment. Candidate generation, metadata regeneration, implementation tests and CI were not executed in this review; their future results remain required by the plan.
independence_basis: The parent authored the revised plan and Design; the user requested the two clarifications. Independent agent /root/independent_delivery_review authored no reviewed contribution, made no engineering edit, reread the complete revised plan and independently reassessed its exact package and changed dependency/traceability allocation.
